A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MVISTA-4D and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–J. Corresponding material can be reliably matched despite repagination and table renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 and the appendices report original generation metrics, manipulation success rates, ablations, and failure analyses on RLBench, RoboTwin, and real-robot data.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds manipulation ablations and inference-efficiency results in Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: v2 introduces +ActionInit, which initializes the trajectory latent from an action-head prediction and uses 10–15 optimization steps, supplementing the retained random-initialization, 100-step procedure. The underlying world model, fusion modules, TCN-VAE, and residual IDM remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RLBench and RoboTwin tasks and 14-task real-robot dataset, with execution results for six real-robot tasks in Table 4. The new experiments use existing simulation coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 5 evaluates manipulation comparators w/o view, w/o mod, w/o view+mod, cat depth, and w/o TCN-VAE; the first two previously appeared only in generation ablations. Table 6 adds +ActionInit. Existing external baselines remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds an offline timing protocol using a shared video backbone on a single H200, separating generation from post-processing time. It also specifies fixed three-view RGB-D inputs for Table 5 and a 10–15-step budget for +ActionInit. Existing training settings and the 100-episode success metric are retained.

E4.justification: Tables 5–6 extend the existing analyses to test fusion and trajectory representation through manipulation success, and action initialization through success and latency. These are targeted additions; the previous inference-mode, camera-embedding, view-count, and failure analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new tables retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing result values are retained. Table 5 adds manipulation-ablation scores. New Table 6 reports +ActionInit success rates of 76.5% and 46.6%, versus the default model's 72.6% and 43.0%, with respective runtimes of 47/84 seconds versus 58/98 seconds. These are additional variant and timing results, not revisions to the original model's scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and the associated mathematical definitions and objectives are unchanged, including camera encoding, trajectory representation, and latent optimization. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: consistent multiview RGB-D prediction, trajectory-latent action inference, residual refinement, and evaluation across 34 tasks. The clarified dataset wording and concluding geometric-interface description restate the existing scope.

C2.justification: v2 attributes cat depth's weaker results to RGB-pretraining and token-position issues, and interprets action-head initialization as providing a better optimization starting point. It also discusses pipeline-specific latency sources. Existing failure explanations and calibration/latency limitations in the appendices are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link, identifies the hardware and timing breakdown for the efficiency experiment, and documents +ActionInit's initialization and iteration count. The detailed implementation and data-collection appendices are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and substantive positioning against previous research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited abstract and conclusion edits, standardizes several headings, updates correspondence and publication information, and adds analysis paragraphs, acknowledgements, and an impact statement. The overall section organization and appendices remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–6, renumbers the existing appendix tables from 5–9 to 7–11, enlarges Figure 2, and repositions some figures and tables. Existing figure content and captions are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, Tables 5–6 provide direct manipulation evidence for additional component choices and absolute inference-cost measurements, improving empirical support and practical transparency. The tested +ActionInit variant partly addresses the acknowledged optimization cost. These gains are limited: the core benchmark evidence is unchanged, and statistical uncertainty and real-time responsiveness remain unestablished.
